system_description.narrative_title: U.S. economic offensive on Iran and its regional market fallout
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is an escalating U.S.-led campaign of economic pressure and sanctions aimed at isolating and crippling Iran's economy, framed by Trump administration rhetoric of 'economic warfare.' That campaign is generating defensive and retaliatory moves across the region (trade embargoes, missile claims, Houthi attacks), slowing/altering traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and driving volatility and price rises in global oil markets while drawing in third-party states and financial hubs. Feedback loops between sanctions, regional security incidents, and energy-market reactions are producing systemic uncertainty and reconfiguration of trade and diplomatic ties.
system_description.scope: U.S. sanctions policy and diplomatic pressure toward Iran; Iran's economy and military/diplomatic responses; regional state actors (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Israel, Oman, Gulf states, non-state actors like Houthis and Hezbollah); maritime transit through the Strait of Hormuz and global oil/energy market responses; financial and trade nodes (Dubai, China buyers) affected by sanctions and embargoes.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical-economic order, centered on international security architecture and the global energy market
adjacent_subsystems: International trade and finance hubs (e.g., Dubai/UAE)

variables.name: Sanctions pressure intensity
variables.description: The aggregate strength and scope of externally imposed economic restrictions designed to reduce a targeted economy's access to markets and revenue.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement stringency
variables.description: The degree to which measures are monitored, implemented, and penalized across jurisdictions and compliance channels.

variables.name: Banking and payment access restriction
variables.description: The extent of limitations on formal banking, correspondent relationships, and payment-rail access for affected actors.

variables.name: Oil transit throughput through key strait
variables.description: The volume rate of hydrocarbon cargo and tanker traffic passing through the strategic maritime chokepoint.

variables.name: Maritime security incident rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of security incidents (attacks, seizures, interdictions) affecting shipping in the region.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price per barrel for crude oil benchmarks that reflects supply–demand balance and risk premia.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability in oil prices as measured by market fluctuations and implied volatility metrics.

variables.name: Perceived supply disruption risk
variables.description: Market and policy actors' subjective assessment of the likelihood and severity of physical or commercial supply interruptions.

variables.name: Rate of trade rerouting and transshipment
variables.description: The proportion of trade flows redirected through alternative routes, intermediaries, or trade channels to avoid restrictions.

variables.name: Financial hub compliance rate
variables.description: The share of major financial centers and intermediaries that adopt, enforce, or facilitate adherence to extraterritorial restrictions.

variables.name: Third‑party import volume of targeted exports
variables.description: The volume of goods and commodities purchased by non-primary actors from the restricted economy despite pressure or prohibition.

variables.name: Energy market liquidity and spare capacity
variables.description: The availability of tradable volumes, spare production/stock capacity, and ease of executing transactions in energy markets.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: The average cost and risk loading for maritime insurance covering vessels and cargo transiting contested waters.

variables.name: Diplomatic alignment cohesion
variables.description: The degree of coordinated diplomatic support or opposition among external actors regarding measures and responses to the crisis.

variables.name: Non‑state maritime attack rate
variables.description: The tempo and severity of offensive actions at sea carried out by irregular or non‑state armed groups affecting commerce.

variables.name: Target economy resilience
variables.description: The capacity of an economy to absorb, adapt to, and recover from sustained external economic pressure and trade disruption.

catalysts.title: U.S. 'toughest' sanctions announced
catalysts.description: Official U.S. announcement/rollout of a new, wide sanctions package targeting Iran and its partners following Bessent/administration statements.
catalysts.rationale: Bessent press conference planned; multiple headlines: 'US will impose "toughest" sanctions', 'Trump vows "crushing economic operation"'.

catalysts.title: Dubai/UAE compliance ramp-up
catalysts.description: Gulf financial hubs (notably Dubai/UAE) increase enforcement/embargo measures, restricting Iranian trade/finance and detaining intermediaries.
catalysts.rationale: 'Plan to Squeeze Iran's Economy Will Live or Die in Dubai'; 'UAE suspends trade'; 'Two Binance employees detained in UAE'.

catalysts.title: Sustained Strait of Hormuz traffic slowdown
catalysts.description: Continued decline in tanker transits through the Strait as shippers avoid the waterway amid security and sanction-related risks.
catalysts.rationale: 'Hormuz traffic slows'; 'Ships passing through Hormuz hover in single digits'; oil price headlines.

catalysts.title: Increase in non-state maritime attacks
catalysts.description: Escalation of Houthi/IRGC-linked and other irregular maritime attacks/seizures affecting commercial shipping and regional security.
catalysts.rationale: 'Iran’s attacks on ships in Hormuz Mounts'; 'Yemen's Houthis say they attacked ... Aramco facilities'.

catalysts.title: China reduces purchases of Iranian oil
catalysts.description: Chinese buyers scale back or delay purchases of Iranian crude as U.S. blockade and pressure make sourcing riskier and costlier.
catalysts.rationale: 'Iranian oil offers to Chinese buyers fall as US blockade bites'; US urging China to cooperate.

catalysts.title: Gulf trade/embargo escalation
catalysts.description: Additional Gulf states follow UAE in suspending trade or imposing embargo measures on Iran, widening regional economic isolation.
catalysts.rationale: 'UAE suspends trade with Iran'; 'UAE severs trade' headlines signal potential contagion to other Gulf actors.

catalysts.title: U.S. push for Chinese cooperation on sanctions
catalysts.description: Diplomatic pressure campaign by U.S. officials aimed at securing Chinese cooperation or acquiescence to tighter Iran economic measures.
catalysts.rationale: 'Bessent says US to impose "toughest" sanctions, urges China to cooperate'; multiple US appeals in headlines.
